general.description: Woody shrub-like photosynthetic organisms adapted to extreme environments. They anchor into rocky terrain using deep root structures and survive strong temperature fluctuations and low-light conditions. Highly widespread across the galaxy.
environmental_context: Found on rocky surfaces with exposed terrain
Some variants appear on high metal content worlds
Often located in low-light or cold environments

color_variants.rule: Color depends on parent star type (applies to all species)

Frutexa flabellum.description: Fan-shaped shrub structure adapted to ammonia-rich environments.

Frutexa flammasis.description: Dense branching structure optimized for ammonia atmospheres.

Frutexa metallicum.description: Heavy, mineral-enriched variant capable of surviving harsh metallic environments.

Frutexa acus.description: Spiny, needle-like structures adapted for CO2-rich cold worlds.

Frutexa fera.description: Wild, sprawling growth pattern found in cold CO2 atmospheres.

Frutexa collum.description: Column-like growth structure thriving in sulphur dioxide atmospheres.

Frutexa sponsae.description: Delicate branching form adapted to water-based atmospheres.

special_rules: Thin atmosphere is mandatory for all species
Atmosphere type is the primary filtering mechanism
High Metal Content worlds only support Frutexa metallicum
Color system is entirely based on parent star type
Rocky terrain is the default habitat for all species
